newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Kurdish leader sees U.N. envoys on Iraqi food plan.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish leader sees U.N. envoys on Iraqi food plan.

text.p: A Kurdish leader complained on Monday that Kurds were not receiving the humanitarian supplies provided under an Iraqi oil-for-food plan, U.N. officials and diplomats said.

Jalal Talabani, secretary-general of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), saw Security Council envoys; U.N. officials in the Department of Humanitarian Affairs, which supervises the plan; and Undersecretary-General Kieran Prendergast, head of the Political Affairs Department.
Under the oil-for-food programme, funds are earmarked for the Kurdish north of the country and are to be distributed by the United Nations rather than Iraq.

The plan allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil every six months to provide goods for its people, suffering under stringent U.N. sanctions imposed seven years ago when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait.
One diplomat said Talabani "complained that Kurds were not getting what they were meant to get in the north under the terms of the plan."
In addition, U.N. officials said, he discussed recent negotiations among rival Kurdish groups and the state of human rights in the north.

Iraq last September helped the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), led by Massoud Barzani, oust the PUK from the city of Arbil. The move prompted the United States to fire missiles against Iraqi air defences in the south.

In a statement, the PUK said Talabani was demanding that Baghdad "cease repression of the Kurdish people." It said Iraq had recently escalated a campaign to deport Kurds and Turkomans from the northern city of Kirkuk and replace them with Arab settlers.
